Amalino: a free talking app (AAC) for children
A free AAC app for children who don't speak yet: tap a picture, hear the word. In English, Danish, Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, Spanish and Lithuanian.
Words for children who don't speak, or don't speak yet
Amalino is an app for phones and tablets. A child taps pictures, and the device says the words out loud, in the family's own language.

I'm making Amalino because some children have a lot to say and no easy way to say it. It's free, it works without the internet, and it speaks for them when they tap pictures, in the languages your family uses at home. Having a voice shouldn't be a privilege.
Amalino isn't in the app stores yet. I'm testing it on real phones and tablets now, and the first families will try it soon.
Would you like to hear when it's ready? Write to me at {email}.
What makes it different
Words stay in their place

The words a child needs most are always in the same place, so their hand learns the way, just as yours does on a keyboard. Start with a few big buttons and show more words as your child grows. Nothing moves.
Your family's languages

English, Danish, Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, Spanish and Lithuanian, with one tap to switch. Ten natural voices speak every one of them: one download, and they work offline. You can also record words in your own voice, so it sounds like home.
Help for the grown-ups
Children learn to talk with pictures the way they learn to talk with words: by watching us. Amalino shows you where each word is and gives short tips, so you can talk with the pictures too.
Private and offline
No account, no ads, no tracking. Amalino works without the internet, and what your child says stays on your device.
Will it stop my child from learning to talk?

No. Research shows that talking with pictures doesn't hold speech back, and it may even help. It's a bridge to talking, not a replacement. There's no minimum age, and a child doesn't have to be "ready" first.
For iPhone, iPad, and Android phones and tablets.
Apart from English, the languages are still a preview, so some words may change.
If you spot a wrong word, tell me at {email}.
Can you help with a language?
Every language in Amalino needs someone who speaks it at home to check the words. If that could be you, have a look.

Why I'm making Amalino
The story behind Amalino: one person making a free AAC app that gives children words in their family's languages. Always free for children and families.
Why I'm making Amalino, a free AAC app for children
I've always believed that technology is at its best when it gives people something they didn't have before. Not another convenience, not another distraction, but something that genuinely matters.

Communication is one of those things we rarely think about until it's difficult. Being able to say what you want, how you feel, or simply "no" is such a basic part of being human. Some children have a lot to say and no easy way to say it. Some don't speak yet, some speak only a few words, and some may never speak much at all. An app that speaks for them when they tap pictures can change their day: they can ask for a drink, say no, make a joke, or tell you what hurts.

I build software and hardware for a living, and I wanted to use those skills to make something useful. When I started exploring AAC apps, the communication apps for people who can't rely on speech, I found that many were expensive, tied to specific devices, or didn't support the languages families speak at home.
That's why I'm making Amalino: a free communication app that works without the internet, because having a voice shouldn't be a privilege.
It's a small contribution to a much bigger problem, but I hope it makes someone's everyday life a little easier. If your child uses Amalino, I'd really love to hear from you.
How I build it

**Research first.** The core words come from studies of what young children really say. About 200 of them cover most of everyday talk, and they keep their place on the screen so a child's hand learns the way.
**Tested on real devices.** I try every change on an iPad, an Android tablet and an older Android phone, to make sure it stays quick. Nothing counts as done until it works on a real device.

**Checked by native speakers.** Danish, Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, Spanish and Lithuanian are drafted with the help of AI translation, and then native speakers check them. Until a native speaker has checked a language, the app marks it as a preview.
**Private from the start.** No account, no ads, no analytics. The app works offline, and anything that needs the internet asks first.

**Grown-ups learn too.** Children learn to talk with pictures by seeing adults use them. So Amalino shows parents where each word is and gives short, friendly tips, without making anyone feel they're doing it wrong.
Amalino is free for children and families, and it will stay that way. There are no ads in it, now or later.
Thank you

A few pictures come from Mulberry Symbols (CC BY-SA) and OpenMoji (CC BY-SA 4.0). The natural voices come from Supertonic 3, shared under the OpenRAIL-M licence. Thank you to everyone who shares their work like this, and to every parent and native speaker who tells me what to fix.

Help translate Amalino
How to help translate Amalino: check a language the app already has, or help add yours. All it takes is a spreadsheet and an email.
Help translate Amalino into your language

A child should be able to talk in the language they hear at home. That's why every word in Amalino needs to be checked by someone who speaks the language, not just by a translation tool. You don't need to be a translator or install anything: a spreadsheet and a little time are enough.
Write to me at {email} and tell me which language you speak.
How it works
Improve a language Amalino already has
Amalino speaks English, Danish, Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, Spanish and Lithuanian. Apart from English, the text is a first draft. The app marks it as a preview until a native speaker has checked it.
I send you a review spreadsheet for your language. Each row has the English, the draft in your language and, for words, the picture.
If a row is right, write "yes" in the "OK?" column. If it isn't, write a better word or sentence in the "Correction" column. Leave it empty if you're not sure.
Send the spreadsheet back. I put your corrections into the app and mark the text as checked.

You don't have to do it all at once. The setup screens and the first words matter most, so they come first. Some languages have a few extra questions, for example about word endings for boys and girls.

Do you use GitHub? Then you can also [[fix a translation there]]: every language has its own file, and I check each change before it goes into the app. A simple web form for translators is coming too.
Add your language
If your language isn't in Amalino yet, you can help bring it in.
I send you a translation spreadsheet: the app's English text, with an empty column for your words. The setup screens and a child's first words come first.
Fill in what you can. Even the first page is a real help.
Send it back. I keep your words as a draft for your language.

To be honest, adding a language to the app takes time. It needs a voice that speaks the language well, and a second person to check the words. Your work is kept safe until then, and it will be the start of your language in Amalino.
Until then, families can still make boards in any language by recording each word in their own voice.
On GitHub you can also [[start your language]] by copying the English file. I check everything before it goes into the app.
Thank you. Every word you check helps a child say what they mean.
How Amalino handles your child's data: no account, no ads, no tracking, and everything is kept on your device.
Privacy in Amalino: no account and no ads
This is a draft. A lawyer will check it before Amalino is released.
Amalino is made for children, so it keeps as little as possible, and keeps it on your device. Here is what that means, in plain words.
In the app
Amalino works without an account and without the internet.
Everything the app keeps is stored on your device, encrypted: the boards, your child's name, the words your child has used, recordings of family voices and photos you add. It is never sent to me.

Backups: On iPhone and iPad, if you back up the device to iCloud or a computer, Amalino's data is included, like any other app's. On Android, Amalino's data is not included in your Google backup and is not copied to a new phone. Amalino also makes a backup every day, but it stays on the device and only opens there. To move to a new device, use "{app:exportBackup}".
There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking.
Amalino only uses the internet if you turn on an optional feature and agree first:

{app:arasaacFull} and "{app:moreSymbolSets}": pictures come from ARASAAC (arasaac.org) and Global Symbols (globalsymbols.com). Amalino downloads their word lists and the pictures you choose, and sends only the words you search for. Nothing about your child is sent.

{app:naturalVoicesHeading} (one download of about 129 MB that covers every language) and the speech recogniser for "{app:aiListen}": these files come from GitHub (github.com), either from Amalino's own copy (github.com/amalino-app/voices) or from the original release. Amalino only downloads them; nothing about your child is sent.
Like any website, the sites above can see your device's internet (IP) address when it connects to them.

{app:syncTitle} and "{app:aiCloud}" (not in the app yet): keeping your own devices in sync (end-to-end encrypted), and AI helpers for grown-ups. Each one will ask you separately, and you can turn it off again.
{app:aiContext} uses only the time of day, for example the food page at lunchtime. It doesn't use your calendar or your location, and Amalino doesn't ask for either.

{app:suggestHotspots} looks at a scene's photo on your device, and only when you choose it. On iPhone and iPad it uses Apple's built-in image recognition (Vision). On Android it uses Google ML Kit. The photo never leaves the device, but under Google's ML Kit terms, ML Kit sends Google anonymous information about how the feature performs and is used. This can't be turned off.

When you edit a word, the "{app:translateWord}" button can fill in the same word in your child's other languages. With "{app:offlineTranslation|label}", this happens on your device. You set it up once for each language, in the language settings. On Android, you download Google's ML Kit translation model for each language once (about 30 MB, after you agree). After that, translation works without the internet, and no words from the app are sent. ML Kit's anonymous information applies here too (see above). On iPhone and iPad (iOS 26 or later), Amalino uses the languages you have downloaded in Apple's Translate settings.
{app:exportBackup} makes a copy protected by a password, which you can keep wherever you like. You can delete everything by uninstalling the app.
What Amalino is not
Amalino helps a child communicate. It doesn't diagnose, monitor or treat any condition.
